source_resources.title: nanoGPT: model.py architecture implementation
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT open source license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, and Day 43-45 attention fundamentals.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original legacy TensorFlow 1.x code; nanoGPT provides clean modern PyTorch equivalent.
Includes advanced production features (RoPE, GQA), but nanoGPT's simplicity is ideal for the core Days 46-48 assembly.

source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Local models and classes in the curriculum mirror nanoGPT semantics directly.
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: model.py: class GPT forward(idx, targets): wte + wpe, Blocks, ln_f, lm_head (returns cross-entropy loss when targets are given)

source_resources.title: Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft, Chapter 3: N-gram Language Models
source_resources.author: Daniel Jurafsky, James H. Martin
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections 3.1-3.4: n-gram counts, maximum-likelihood estimation, Laplace smoothing, and perplexity
license_restrictions: Draft text is not reproduced; linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external hyperlink to the authors' public draft PDF; all curriculum explanations are original text.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standard reference text for n-gram definitions, count normalization, smoothing, and perplexity used across Day 38.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on the author's Stanford site; chapter numbering and content may shift between drafts.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All formulas and worked tables in the curriculum are self-contained and verified by execution.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Chen & Goodman: An Empirical Study of Smoothing Techniques for Language Modeling
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Detailed smoothing survey but far beyond the add-one scope of a first n-gram day; optional further reading.
Solid academic lecture treatment but less current and less integrated with executable count tables than the SLP3 draft.
